open_points.subject: A16 rule 1 request-size check
open_points.text: "its size, counted as the bytes of the request message as received, is within `surface_request_bytes_max`"
open_points.question: What exact byte sequence is measured for MCP requests: transport/frame bytes, decoded JSON request bytes, or only the operation payload fields?
options: Count full on-wire MCP frame/message bytes exactly as received
Count decoded JSON request object bytes after transport framing is removed
Count only the operation argument payload bytes
open_points.default_guess: Count decoded JSON request object bytes, excluding MCP transport framing.

open_points.subject: A08 rule 5 + A09 rule 1 `api_base_url` shape
open_points.text: "`api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host counts as none" and "The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path"
open_points.question: Which additional URL components are allowed in `api_base_url` (path prefix, query, fragment, userinfo), and how must they be handled when building the final request URL?
options: Allow only origin form (`scheme://host[:port]`) with no path/query/fragment/userinfo
Allow an optional path prefix but forbid query/fragment/userinfo
Allow any absolute URL and concatenate path literally
open_points.default_guess: Allow optional path prefix, forbid query/fragment/userinfo, then append declared path.

open_points.subject: A09 rule 2 multipart value parts
open_points.text: "a `multipart/form-data` body with one part per other input port ... a value part carrying its canonical JSON"
open_points.question: What `Content-Type` is sent for multipart value parts, and is it part of approval digest matching?
options: Set value parts with no explicit part content-type
Set `text/plain` for scalar values and `application/json` for complex values
open_points.default_guess: Set `application/json` for all value parts and include that media type in request description/digest.

open_points.subject: A10 rule 7 approval `request_digest` header set
open_points.text: "every header the kernel sends, names lower-cased and in code-point order, each with its value, except that the credential header appears by name only"
open_points.question: Does "every header the kernel sends" include library/runtime-added transport headers (e.g., `Host`, `Content-Length`, `User-Agent`) or only headers explicitly set by kernel rules?
options: Include only headers explicitly set by kernel logic (required headers, credential header name, content-type, accept-encoding)
Include all headers present on the final wire request, including client-added defaults
Include required+credential only, excluding protocol/transport headers
open_points.default_guess: Include only headers explicitly set by kernel logic, not client-library implicit defaults.
